semanticRole.roomRole: seating that frames the Temple nave and reinforces sacred civic scale
semanticRole.gameplayRole: collision-only atmospheric fixture; supports center-aisle flow without becoming an interaction target
semanticRole.worldLanguage: Temple of the Dawn civic-sacred interior

allowed: broad wooden seat and backrest silhouettes
low-poly proportions that read at player camera distance
forbidden: ornament added to compensate for weak silhouette
high-contrast stripes that make the pews busier than the altar
tiny repeated detail that reads as visual noise
toy-like end blocks or barricade-like massing

placementRules: rows must leave a clear center aisle
pews should feel subordinate to the room massing and altar
repeat spacing should look like intentional seating rhythm, not a grid of obstacles

rules: aisle must remain visibly processional from the player-spawn camera
row pitch must make seating rhythm legible without forming a tight obstacle grid
the altar sightline must remain open above and between the pew rows

hierarchy.contrastGuidance: Pew value contrast should be lower than altar cloth, stained glass, exit glow, NPCs, and interaction prompts.

rules: wood material must not overpower stained glass or altar
material variation should clarify form rather than create striping
future texture work should use an approved material or trim-sheet path before room integration

cameraEvidence.purpose: prove object reads as pew without room context
prove silhouette is furniture, not barricade/fence
prove pew rows frame the nave and stay subordinate to altar/glass
prove row repetition reads as seating rhythm from reviewer camera

standalone: reads as a pew from front, side, and three-quarter views
does not rely on ornate micro-detail to explain itself
player scale reference makes seat/back height plausible
integrated: frames the nave without competing with altar or stained glass
row rhythm supports the center aisle
wood/material contrast is quieter than focal sacred elements
does not read as fence, crate, barricade, or repeated obstacle grid from Temple nave screenshots
play: collider footprint prevents clipping without snagging the center aisle
does not block or confuse the intended Temple flow

currentDiagnosis: current candidate reads as a pew but looks like it is trying too hard
material and rail contrast make repeated rows visually busier than the room can support
the asset needs calmer silhouette/material decisions before another geometry-detail pass

nextProductionPass.preferredHypothesis: Simpler pew geometry plus quieter wood hierarchy will improve representational sanity more than adding detail.
